name: Arthur Baker
hook: The producer who welded Kraftwerk to a Roland drum machine and got sued for it.
blurb: Baker had studied engineering before he moved to New York in 1981 and started working at Tommy Boy Records. The next year he produced "Planet Rock" with Afrika Bambaataa, with John Robie playing synthesizers, and it was put together methodically: the Kraftwerk parts were played again by studio musicians rather than sampled, which shaped the legal dispute that followed. He kept making electro and dance records through the eighties, and later produced for Bruce Springsteen and New Order, a sign of how quickly electro and hip-hop production methods crossed over into the wider pop business.

signatureTracks.title: Planet Rock (Afrika Bambaataa and the Soulsonic Force)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Baker's production, with John Robie on synthesizers,, built around interpolated Kraftwerk parts and an 808, is the record that defined electro.
